steps.text: Near the coast, the wind changes direction between day and night. It's convection on a giant scale. Let's see why.
Set the time to daytime and watch the breeze.
By day, land heats up faster than the sea. Hot air over land rises, and cool air blows in from the sea — a sea breeze.
At night it flips: land cools faster than the sea, so air flows from land to sea — a land breeze. Same rule: cool air moves toward the warmer side.

coach.mission: Find out why the breeze blows one way by day and the other by night.
whenStuck: Switch between day and night and watch which way the breeze blows.
Ask: which heats or cools faster — land or sea?
whenWrong: Day: land heats faster → sea breeze (from sea to land). Night: land cools faster → land breeze.
Cool air always moves toward the warmer side.
whenCorrect: Right — by day the cooler sea air blows onto the warmer land.
Good — at night it reverses into a land breeze.
coach.done: You've seen how land and sea breezes form. Explore more, or move on when you're ready.
